title: Add BASE_DEFAULT_VALS
description:
BASE_DEFAULT_VALS provides improved fidelity to define names for unused or illegal
ranges of values for enumerations than the standard "Unknown".  In some rarer
instances, there may be data that maps a boolean to a single value in an 8-bit range
and all other values in the range to the other.

notes.body: One problem is: struct _value_string . value is of type uint32_t. That doesn't work well with -1.

Thanks for the feedback.  Is there an alternate form that would get more traction?

Could use a "named constant" of some form that points to UINT32_MAX, but what to call it and where to place it (in proto.h probably) I'm not sure.

I'll try to come up with something, but would a named constant for UINT32_MAX be more acceptable?

There isn't an obvious equivalent of an integer type with an out-of-band sentinel value in C that would not also potentially impact the definition of struct _value_string.

Best regards,
John D.

I'll add this one last thing.  If one were to suggest using int32_t instead of uint32_t for the index into struct _value_string to get a legitimate sentinel value for -1, is that an acceptable compromise?  Regardless, I can only provide the concept of the idea; I don't have the authority to re-architect the feature into the mainline repository.  In my personal fork, I find the feature to be very useful in dissecting MIL-STD-1553 data over ethernet.

The underlying question is always, in-band or out-of-band. Since we make no reservations on the values in the value_string (except type uint32_t), in-band is always going to cause trouble. Unless we concoct some clever extension ot value_string, and figure out how that's going to compete with val_to_str() function calls, this may not work.

I agree that ideally the information should be "out-of-band".  In the header info struct, you kind of manage this with an out-of-band declaration of internal data in the structure using HFILL.  Not sure if something can be created like struct _ext_value_string that can be keyed when using the "BASE_DEFAULT_VALS" flag.  The "strings" field already is used in a slightly "unholy" way, so keying off a new structure when that flag is detected could potentially play nice with the existing infrastructure.

There is the "C struct hack" technique to append a variable length data to an existing structure using the allocator.  Doesn't seem like it would be the tool of choice to solve this conundrum.

Just a couple thoughts.

                   BASE_CUSTOM, or BASE_NONE, possibly ORed with
                   BASE_RANGE_STRING, BASE_EXT_STRING, BASE_VAL64_STRING,
                   BASE_ALLOW_ZERO, BASE_UNIT_STRING, BASE_SPECIAL_VALS,
-                  BASE_NO_DISPLAY_VALUE, BASE_SHOW_ASCII_PRINTABLE, or
-                  BASE_SHOW_UTF_8_PRINTABLE
+                  BASE_NO_DISPLAY_VALUE, BASE_SHOW_ASCII_PRINTABLE, 
+                  BASE_SHOW_UTF_8_PRINTABLE, or BASE_DEFAULT_VALS
 
                   BASE_NONE may be used with a non-NULL FIELDCONVERT when the
                   numeric value of the field itself is not of significance to
@@ -157,8 +157,8 @@ FIELDDISPLAY    --For FT_UINT{8,16,24,32,40,48,56,64} and
 
                 --For FT_CHAR:
                   BASE_HEX, BASE_OCT, BASE_CUSTOM, or BASE_NONE, possibly
-                  ORed with BASE_RANGE_STRING, BASE_EXT_STRING or
-                  BASE_VAL64_STRING.
+                  ORed with BASE_RANGE_STRING, BASE_EXT_STRING, 
+                  BASE_VAL64_STRING, or BASE_DEFAULT_VALS.
 
                   BASE_NONE can be used in the same way as with FT_UINT8.
 
@@ -1114,6 +1114,20 @@ then just the numeric value is displayed (i.e. no "Unknown"). This is
 intended for use when the value_string only gives special names for
 certain field values and values not in the value_string are expected.
 
+If BASE_DEFAULT_VALS is also applied to the display bitmask, then if the
+numeric value of a field doesn't match any values in the value_string then
+the string for the numeric value -1 is displayed. This is intended for use
+when the value_string only gives special names for certain field values 
+and a default name for the rest. The value -1 is an arbitrary numeric
+value that is not expected to be part of the normal range of values, e.g.
+
+    static const value_string valstringname[] = {
+        { -1,      "Default String" },
+        { INTVAL1, "Descriptive String 1" },
+        { INTVAL2, "Descriptive String 2" },
+        { 0,       NULL }
+    };
+
 -- Extended value strings
 You can also use an extended version of the value_string for faster lookups.
 It requires a value_string array as input.

@@ -743,9 +743,11 @@ typedef enum {
 
 #define BASE_SPECIAL_VALS         0x00008000  /**< field will not display "Unknown" if value_string match is not found */
 
-#define BASE_SHOW_ASCII_PRINTABLE 0x00010000 /**< show byte array as ASCII if it's all printable characters */
+#define BASE_SHOW_ASCII_PRINTABLE 0x00010000  /**< show byte array as ASCII if it's all printable characters */
 
-#define BASE_SHOW_UTF_8_PRINTABLE 0x00020000 /**< show byte array as UTF-8 if it's all valid and printable UTF-8 characters */
+#define BASE_SHOW_UTF_8_PRINTABLE 0x00020000  /**< show byte array as UTF-8 if it's all valid and printable UTF-8 characters */
+
+#define BASE_DEFAULT_VALS         0x00080000  /**< field will use -1 value instead of "Unknown" if value_string match is not found */
 
 /** BASE_ values that cause the field value to be displayed twice */
 #define IS_BASE_DUAL(b) ((b)==BASE_DEC_HEX||(b)==BASE_HEX_DEC)
